projectBackground.name: 120 MW Solar Park — Site Screening
projectBackground.context: Three candidate sites must be screened on yield and cost before land options are signed.

manager.name: Lucía Fernández
manager.note: Lenders ask three questions: how much energy, at what cost and how sure are you. Answer all three.

assignment.title: Screen the solar sites
assignment.brief: Calculate yield, capacity factor and cost per MWh, compare sites in Excel and write the committee note.

documents.name: Site A Data
documents.note: 10 MWp; specific yield 1,800 kWh/kWp; performance ratio 0.80.

documents.name: Site Comparison
documents.note: Three sites with size, yield and performance ratio.

tasks.title: Annual Energy
tasks.prompt: 10,000 kWp x 1,800 kWh/kWp x performance ratio 0.80. What is annual energy in MWh?
tasks.reasoning: Yield = capacity x specific yield x PR.
tasks.tip: State the source of irradiation data.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Capacity Factor
tasks.prompt: 10 MW produces 14,400 MWh per year. What is the capacity factor (%) over 8,760 hours?
tasks.reasoning: Capacity factor compares actual to maximum output.
tasks.mistake: Using 24x365 incorrectly is common; hours are 8,760.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Simple Cost per MWh
tasks.prompt: (Capex 8,000,000 + opex 100,000 x 20) / (14,400 MWh x 20). What is the cost (€ per MWh)?
tasks.reasoning: Levelised cost spreads total cost over total energy.
tasks.tip: A full LCOE discounts cost and energy.
tasks.mistake: Using year-one energy only against 20-year cost doubles the answer.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Degradation
tasks.prompt: Panels lose about 0.5% output per year. What must the model include?
options: Annual degradation applied to yield over the project life
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Site Comparison (Excel)
tasks.prompt: Annual energy in MWh (D = B x C x E / 1000, where E is the performance ratio). Upload for checking.
tasks.reasoning: The biggest site is not the best per kWp.
tasks.mistake: Judging by capacity alone hides poor yield.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Committee Note
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence note to the investment committee.
tasks.modelAnswer: Site 3 produces the most energy at 15,744 MWh a year but Site 2 delivers the best yield per kWp at 1,900. For the reference 10 MWp design, we expect 14,400 MWh a year at about €35 per MWh before financing. Key risks are irradiation uncertainty and degradation, which our P90 case captures. I recommend securing options on Sites 2 and 3 and commissioning a bankable yield study.
tasks.reasoning: A good note gives the key numbers, the risk and a clear recommendation.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Optimistic Yield
caseStudy.background: A project was financed on a P50 yield with no uncertainty analysis. Actual output was 9% lower and debt service coverage fell below 1.0.
caseStudy.challenges: Only one yield estimate was used.
caseStudy.constraints: Irradiation data was from a single year.
caseStudy.solution: Voltara adopted P50 and P90 yields for all financial models.
